notes: v10.4 BUILD REFRESH (2026-11-15, b4755 — the eighteenth cut — a web address is never an email; a word is only swapped for one that sounds like it; one address is written once, notarized): (1) A web address is no longer turned into an email address. "Create a new page at www.example.com forward slash BB" was pasted as "page@www.example.com": since August, any word followed by "at" and a domain was assembled as an email address. An address that opens with "www", or that is followed by a path, is a website, and "at" stays a word. "John at example.com" still becomes an email address. (2) A word is only replaced by one that sounds like it. A rule that replaces a capitalised word you have never used with a similar word from your own vocabulary turned "Sonor" into "Silero", because their consonants were one letter apart. The replacement now also needs the same number of syllables and near-identical consonants, and the rule stands down when the unknown word sits beside a word that begins the s
